meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('absolute, complete').

examples.text: Молчать, я требую абсолютного спокойствия на кухне.
examples.trans: Be quiet, I demand absolute calm in the kitchen.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'without' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

достать.gloss: to take out, to get, to reach

meanings.en: to take out, to pull out, to reach
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take out, to get, to reach', paired with 'доставать'.

meanings.en: to get hold of, to obtain
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take out, to get, to reach', paired with 'доставать'.

examples.trans: And take his eye out with a spoon.
He took his phone out of his pocket.

examples.text: Вы понимаете, что вы нас достали уже?
examples.trans: Do you understand that you've made us sick of you already?

meanings.note: жить на зарплату = to live on one's salary

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович учёный, и он живёт на зарплату.
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich is a scholar, and he lives on a salary.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'кормить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to feed'.

examples.trans: The cook fed the guests deliciously.

examples.text: Раз не можем напоить, мы его накормим!
examples.trans: Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!

examples.text: Мы накормим его вкусным горячим обедом.
examples.trans: We will feed him a delicious hot lunch.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.trans: I will explain everything to you right now.

meanings.note: A door, a window. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'slave', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I have had enough of this slave driver!

meanings.note: 'через полгода' = in six months. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лгода'). Common masculine noun meaning 'half a year, six months' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been here for six months now.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоянно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: What are you constantly afraid of?
He was constantly late for work.
What are you constantly afraid of, Kostik?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'madman' in everyday Russian.
работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Money, things, people. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обрать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to collect, to gather', paired with 'собирать'.

'собрать вещи' = to pack. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обрать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to collect, to gather', paired with 'собирать'.

examples.text: Мэр куда-то спрятал деньги. Местные чиновники не могут собрать нужную сумму.
examples.trans: The mayor has hidden the money somewhere. The local officials can't put together the sum they need.

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: посчитать / сосчитать are the perfectives

Я считаю, что... = I think that. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'читать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to count; to think, to consider', paired with 'посчитать'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: + genitive singular: три дня. Core Russian num meaning 'three' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We give him three days. That's it.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
